egyptian/head-of-merytaten-smk-cast.title: Head of a Queen, possibly Kiya or Meritaten
egyptian/head-of-merytaten-smk-cast.note: Original identified as Berlin ÄM 21245, rather than ÄM 21223. The title preserves the museum’s attribution uncertainty; the historic URL is retained.

asia/coin-die-bahadur-shah-ii.title: Coin Die for Akbar Shah II and Jai Singh III
asia/coin-die-bahadur-shah-ii.note: Exact model UID27e6eca9a96848e4b8e5a530fb66cc04 now identifies Akbar Shah II and Jai Singh III. The inherited Bahadur Shah II title is withdrawn.

modern/smid-ceramic-mosaic.title: Tree-shaped Ceramic Entrance Relief
modern/smid-ceramic-mosaic.note: Atrium localrender and primary survey photographDSC_9210.JPG visually match the distinctive projecting quarter-circle tiles of the entrance tree. Survey11977 attributes this to Milan Chlíbec. Earlier Šmíd attribution conflates it with a separate courtyard relief at the same school.

asia/ganesha-mia.note: The museum record and museum-authored scan identify accession2003.198. The inherited2002.31.1 accession was incorrect. Both existing scan pages are retained.

americas/key-marco-cat.note: The exact Smithsonian model document identifies NMNH anthropology record 8061963. Its official record lists USNM A240915-0 and accession 048531; replace the inconsistent inherited A240915 / E048570 string.

asia/ritual-wine-ewer-gong-smithsonian.note: The current Smithsonian Voyager document explicitly identifies F1961.33a-b. The earlier physical-dimensions entry incorrectly cited a different ewer, F1939.53a-b; the catalog abbreviated F1961.33. Restore the complete accession and linked object record. Older embedded and current bulk dimensional values remain distinct pending calibration review.

americas/hope-school-desk-nmaahc.note: The exact Voyager document collection.edanRecordId identifies nmaahc_2010.22.5, and the linked official object record supplies this accession and dimensions. The local catalog and derivative filename instead say 2010.22.6. This proposal follows the explicit linked collection record, but retains the filename conflict in research evidence and withholds calibration pending identity resolution.

michelangelo/prisoner.title: Young Slave
michelangelo/prisoner.note: Visually matched raised arm, concealed face and unfinished rear block; keep route stable.

donatello/john-the-baptist-as-a-boy.note: Official source attributes the original to Benedetto; historical attribution to Donatello explains existing route. Keep route stable.

aphrodite-anadyomene.title: Esquiline Venus (Aphrodite Anadyomene)
aphrodite-anadyomene.note: Model features and SMK original provenance confirm this unique original.

modern/torso-callender-saam.note: The catalog explicitly identifies Bessie Stough Callender and the United States. The modern collection folder currently overrides that context and files Torso in Europe. The Americas wing already includes American sculptors working in European traditions.

modern/venus-jim-dine-sixth-avenue.note: Jim Dine’s contemporary New York public sculpture is filed in Europe solely through modern. Its current title, maker, geography and exact plaza source support the Americas, irrespective of its quotation of Venus de Milo.

medieval/birds-with-foliage-mosaic-mia.note: Mia’s exact object API identifies Roman nationality, Byzantine style and Byzantine Empire (Antioch), dated late fourth to mid-fifth century. File with the companion Antioch mosaic Elephant Attacking a Feline, already in Greece & Rome, and describe the wing as extending into late antiquity. A medieval folder is insufficient grounds to split these closely related works.

modern/puck-harriet-hosmer-walker-threed.note: Older inconsistency exposed by the review: Hosmer’s Puck is in Europe through modern, while her Zenobia in Chains has an explicit Americas override. Both are works by the American sculptor made in Rome; the present museum’s location should not determine the wing.

asia/mamluk-door-panel-mia.note: Mia’s exact object API records Egypt and Africa. Group this fourteenth-century Mamluk panel with the newly acquired Islamic Egyptian woodwork and monuments already in Africa. This follows geographic wings plus cross-wing Islamic exhibits, and requires revising Asia’s old claim to encompass the whole Islamic world.

ancient-near-east/stargazer-cleveland.note: The old explicit override deliberately put this Western Anatolian statuette in Greece & Rome. Current Cleveland evidence identifies early Bronze Age Western Anatolia, Near Eastern collection, Egyptian and Ancient Near Eastern department, and Ancient Near East gallery. Returning it to the Near East better fits that identity; remove the obsolete legacy-list entry/comment describing an Anatolian Neolithic grouping.
